text:
Kevin Ng: Quick follow-up to the RFC — proposing a lightweight 'tombstone' protocol for retiring API endpoints and a client signal path so integrators can opt-in to faster removals. Thoughts?

Maria Lopez: Can you sketch how the signal actually flows? is this header-based, webhook, or both?

Kevin Ng: Header-first, optional webhook. idea: servers start sending a tombstone header and clear telemetry; clients can choose to surface a deprecation banner. Example header: `X-API-Tombstone: v2; retire-on=2026-08-01; notice=beta`

Samir Patel: How do we measure uptake? we need concrete telemetry to gate hard removals. Have a minimum-uptake policy in mind?

Kevin Ng: yes — propose telemetry events: `tombstone.received`, `tombstone.ack`, `tombstone.migrate`. Gate: >= 80% ack within 90 days before enforcing 429 -> 410 transition. ops will get a metric per-tenant.

Ashley Chen: UI/console questions: do we expose a tenant opt-out for longer retention? also want an admin API to extend per-tenant windows.

Kevin Ng: propose admin API `/admin/tombstone/{tenant}` with PATCH body { "extend_until": "2026-12-01", "reason": "legal" }. defaults: 90 day grace + 30 day soft-penalty (warn/request quota reduction).

Samir Patel: What about shims? we still need a runtime fallback path for clients that don't migrate. Do we create a compatibility proxy or prefer server-side adapters?

Kevin Ng: prefer server-side adapters for short term (configurable per-tenant), and long-term encourage client migration. adapters will emit a per-request header `X-Compat-Proxy: true` so metrics separate. Sidecar/proxy is opt-in via tenant config.

Maria Lopez: rollout plan? sequence of states would help ops and support docs.

Kevin Ng: rough plan: 1) broadcast tombstone header (informational) + console banners (day 0) 2) collect telemetry for 90 days 3) mark endpoints as soft-limited -> 429 to unacknowledged clients (30d) 4) enforce 410 for non-compliant (final). Provide per-tenant extension via admin API and automated canary that tests migration for top-50 tenants first.

Ashley Chen: Any risk of false positives (third-party SDKs that don't propagate headers)? we need detection heuristics.

Samir Patel: add a heuristic: if `tombstone.received` counts but `tombstone.ack` is near zero and user-agent matches our SDK list, route detail to SDK team as a regression. Also flag requests with `X-Forwarded-For` from known CDNs for additional checks.

Kevin Ng: agreement on telemetry + heuristics. I'll draft the protocol doc and a minimal admin API spec. Also one concrete swagger snippet to start: ```json
{
  "path": "/admin/tombstone/{tenant}",
  "methods": ["GET","PATCH"],
  "patch": {"extend_until": "string(ISO8601)", "contact": "string"}
}
```

infra-bot: deploy-bot triggered: canary rollout job queued for `tombstone-proto/v1` -> job id `deploy-2026-1183` :rocket:

Maria Lopez: thanks — please include sample client code for acknowledging the tombstone header in the doc. small snippet like `if (resp.headers['x-api-tombstone']) ack()` would be enough.

Kevin Ng: will do. I'll post the draft RFC link in #eng-infra when ready and cc @Ashley Chen for admin API UX. 

Ashley Chen: ping me when the admin API spec is up. we'll want a simple console flow to request extensions and show countdowns.

Samir Patel: also add a periodic report exported to support for tenants in the final 30d. makes triage easier.

Kevin Ng: noted — adding export. thanks all.
